question: Where can a mathematical object stop behaving smoothly?
idea: A solution or shape may be well-behaved in some places and irregular in others. Understanding those irregularities helps distinguish a controlled solution from a possible breakdown. This entry studies the particular situation described below.
why: The study of shapes defined by equations, often using complex numbers. It connects geometric features with algebraic rules.

glossary.meaning: A place where an object or solution fails to have the expected smooth or regular behavior.

exactClaim: Proves topological right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in ℂ3 with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the μ-constant problem. After shrinking the parameter disk and representatives, ambient homeomorphisms vary jointly continuously, fix the origin section and preserve the defining functions.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
